mainEntity.name: How much does a Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi engine (D4FD) costs £400-£1,200 supply-only, while a reconditioned unit is £1,200-£2,200 and a full rebuilt engine £2,000-£3,800 [EM-QUOTE]. Fitted costs add £520-£650 labour at a specialist. Compare quotes through EnginesMarket to find the best deal for your exact year and mileage.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of DMF failure in a Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Symptoms include clutch judder when pulling away, metallic rattling on startup, and vibration through the clutch pedal. If you hear a "knocking" sound at idle that disappears when the clutch is depressed, that's also a classic DMF warning sign. These failures typically occur between 80,000-120,000 miles [THIRD-PARTY].

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt D4FD engine costs around £2,000-£3,800 supply-only [EM-QUOTE]. For a 2011-2014 i40 worth £3,000-£6,000, replacement may represent 50-80% of vehicle value - often borderline. For a 2016+ facelift i40 worth £6,000-£9,000, replacement is more financially sensible. Always factor in labour (£520-£650) and the value of a 12-month warranty vs. scrapping.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A specialist workshop typically completes a full D4FD engine swap in 8-10 hours. With parts sourcing and delivery factored in, allow 2-3 days from quote to car back on the road. Supply & fit options through EnginesMarket streamline the process by pairing you with a specialist who has the engine in stock.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi 116 and the 136/141 versions?

acceptedAnswer.text: All three use the same D4FD engine block, but with different ECU mapping and sometimes slightly different injectors. The 116hp (85kW) was the original launch variant (2011-2015), the 136hp (100kW) arrived in 2012, and the 141hp (104kW) was introduced with the 2015 facelift. All are compatible with the same core replacement engine - the supplier will match the correct ECU tune to your vehicle [THIRD-PARTY].

mainEntity.name: Does the Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi uses a timing chain, not a belt [THIRD-PARTY]. This is confirmed by main dealers and owners' forums. The chain does not need routine replacement like a belt, but can stretch on higher-mileage examples (100k+). A rattling noise at startup or unusual diesel knock can indicate chain wear - which a specialist should inspect immediately [EM-INTERVIEW].

historyTimeline.h2: Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi launched in 2011 as the diesel mainstay of Hyundai's mid-size family car range. Built around the D4FD engine, it evolved through three power outputs before production ended in 2019, with the Tourer continuing until 2020.

milestones.description: D4FD, 1.7-litre, 116hp (85kW) - launch variant, also known as the 1.7 CRDi 116
D4FD, 1.7-litre, 136hp (100kW) - high-output variant introduced, frequently badged as Premium or Style
D4FD, 1.7-litre, 141hp (104kW) - facelift variant introduced alongside the refreshed i40, replacing the 136hp version
End of production for the i40 saloon; Tourer continued until 2020

commonProblems.h2: Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi (D4FD) has three dominant failure points that drive replacement decisions: DMF failure, DPF blockage, and timing chain stretch. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Dual Mass Flywheel Failure - Why the Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi D4FD Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The DMF is designed to smooth engine vibrations but wears due to the diesel engine's torque characteristics. Symptoms include clutch judder, metallic rattling on startup, and vibration through the pedal [THIRD-PARTY].

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace dual mass flywheel and clutch assembly
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if DMF is the only issue; usually 100,000-mile lifespan

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When DMF failure has caused further engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2014-2016 i40 1.7 CRDi with 80k-100k miles is worth approximately £3,000-£8,000 [THIRD-PARTY][INDUSTRY ESTIMATE]. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: DMF replacement makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: For a high-mileage i40 (120k+), a full rebuilt engine with updated components can be more cost-effective than repeated repairs if the DMF has failed and caused collateral damage. If the car is worth under £4,000 and the DMF has failed without further engine damage, a specialist DMF replacement is the more sensible financial decision [EM-INTERVIEW].
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt D4FD Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi engine prices

problems.h4: DPF Blockage - Why the Hyundai i40 1.7 CRDi D4FD Fails in Urban Use
problems.rootCause: Short urban journeys prevent the DPF from reaching the required temperature for active regeneration. Soot accumulates, triggering warning lights, reduced power, and limp mode. In some cases, failed DPF regens lead to oil dilution with fuel [EM-INTERVIEW][THIRD-PARTY].

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Professional DPF cleaning, often with a forced regeneration [THIRD-PARTY]
repairOptions.longevity: First port of call for blockage; effective if caught early
When DPF damage has caused engine oil dilution or injector issues

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2011-2013 i40 1.7 CRDi with 100k+ miles is worth approximately £3,000-£6,000 [THIRD-PARTY][INDUSTRY ESTIMATE].
problems.recommendation: If your i40 1.7 CRDi is used mainly for urban trips, a professional DPF clean is usually the best first step [EM-INTERVIEW]. Regular motorway driving (30+ minutes at 2,000rpm+) allows passive regeneration and extends DPF life. If oil dilution has occurred (indicated by rising oil level), investigate immediately - it can lead to engine damage [EM-INTERVIEW][THIRD-PARTY].
